## Purpose and Build Surface
Wicked Engine is a C++17 cross-platform 3D engine, embeddable framework, standalone scene editor, and Lua-scriptable runtime. The root build entry is `CMakeLists.txt`; the Windows solution is `WickedEngine.sln`. The engine is exposed as a static-library-style API through `WickedEngine/WickedEngine.h` and built by `WickedEngine/CMakeLists.txt`.

## Application Entry Points
The primary shipped application is the editor, with platform launchers at `Editor/main_Windows.cpp`, `Editor/main_SDL2.cpp`, and `Editor/main_MacOS.mm`; its orchestration class is `Editor/Editor.cpp`. Consumer application templates start in `Samples/Template_Windows/main.cpp`, `Samples/Template_Linux/main.cpp`, or Apple/iOS equivalents. All host applications create `wi::Application`, attach a native window, activate a render path, then repeatedly run the engine frame loop.

## Runtime Orchestration and UI
`WickedEngine/wiApplication.cpp` is the lifecycle boundary: initialization, window/frame execution, active render-path management, and engine subsystem coordination. Render paths separate application presentation from engine rendering: `WickedEngine/wiRenderPath.h`, `WickedEngine/wiRenderPath2D.cpp`, and `WickedEngine/wiRenderPath3D.cpp`. Editor tools operate on that runtime through docking-style component windows, notably `Editor/Editor.cpp`, `Editor/HierarchyWindow.cpp`, and `Editor/ComponentsWindow.cpp`.

## Scene, ECS, Assets, and Import
The scene layer owns entities, components, serialization, and scene composition: `WickedEngine/wiScene.h`, `WickedEngine/wiScene_Components.cpp`, and `WickedEngine/wiScene_Serializers.cpp`. WISCENE is the native persisted scene format; `Content/models/*.wiscene` are runtime/editor inputs. The editor imports external OBJ, FBX, glTF/GLB, and PLY into scene data via `Editor/ModelImporter.h`, `Editor/ModelImporter_GLTF.cpp`, and `Editor/ModelImporter_FBX.cpp`. Resource loading/caching is bounded through `WickedEngine/wiResourceManager.cpp`.

## Rendering and GPU Boundary
`WickedEngine/wiRenderer.cpp` converts scene state into GPU work; `WickedEngine/wiGraphicsDevice.h` is the graphics abstraction. Concrete backends are DirectX 12 (`WickedEngine/wiGraphicsDevice_DX12.cpp`), Vulkan (`WickedEngine/wiGraphicsDevice_Vulkan.cpp`), and Metal (`WickedEngine/wiGraphicsDevice_Metal.cpp`), selected by platform/arguments. HLSL shader sources and CPU/GPU shared layouts reside in `WickedEngine/shaders/`—for example `WickedEngine/shaders/ShaderInterop_Renderer.h`, `WickedEngine/shaders/objectPS.hlsl`, and `WickedEngine/shaders/tonemapCS.hlsl`. Shader compilation is encapsulated by `WickedEngine/wiShaderCompiler.cpp` and the offline compiler entry `WickedEngine/offlineshadercompiler.cpp`.

## Simulation, Effects, and Media
Physics is integrated through the engine-facing boundary `WickedEngine/wiPhysics_Jolt.cpp` and embedded Jolt implementation under `WickedEngine/Jolt/Physics/PhysicsSystem.cpp`; scene components feed bodies/constraints and simulation results return to transforms. GPU-driven effects are first-class renderer inputs, including emitted particles (`WickedEngine/wiEmittedParticle.cpp`), hair (`WickedEngine/wiHairParticle.cpp`), ocean (`WickedEngine/wiOcean.cpp`), terrain, voxel grids, and Gaussian splats. Audio and video services are provided by `WickedEngine/wiAudio.cpp` and `WickedEngine/wiVideo.cpp`; bundled FAudio supports audio on applicable platforms.

## Scripting, Input, and Platform Services
Lua is embedded in `WickedEngine/LUA/` and surfaced through `WickedEngine/wiLua.cpp`; `*_BindLua.cpp` files expose application, scene, render, input, audio, physics, and resource APIs. Scripts can control the same global/separate scenes and render paths used by C++. Input is abstracted in `WickedEngine/wiInput.cpp`, with SDL and platform-specific providers including `WickedEngine/wiSDLInput.cpp`. External runtime dependencies/infrastructure are primarily native graphics APIs, SDL2 on Linux, Apple Metal frameworks, Vulkan, and DX12 rather than networked services.
